title: Fixed-parameter tractability of graph isomorphism by rank-width
formal: Do there exist one deterministic multitape Turing machine \(A\), a total computable function \(f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N_{\ge1}\), and an integer \(c\ge1\) such that, for every pair of finite simple undirected graphs \(G,H\), \(A\) decides whether \(G\cong H\) within \[f(k)(|V(G)|+|V(H)|+2)^c\] bit operations, where \(k=\max\{\operatorname{rw}(G),\operatorname{rw}(H)\}\)? Graphs are supplied by their explicitly encoded adjacency matrices; neither a rank decomposition nor a width bound is supplied.
definitions:
A graph of order \(n\ge0\) has vertex set \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \([0]=\varnothing\), and an \(n\times n\) symmetric zero-one adjacency matrix with zero diagonal. Thus there are no loops, parallel edges, colors or vertex labels that an isomorphism must preserve. For graphs of orders \(n,m\), the assertion \(G\cong H\) means that there is a bijection \(\pi:[n]\to[m]\) satisfying
\[
\{u,v\}\in E(G)\ \Longleftrightarrow\
\{\pi(u),\pi(v)\}\in E(H)
\quad\text{for every }u,v\in[n].
\]
The required output is one decision bit; an isomorphism, canonical labeling or canonical graph is not required.

For \(X\subseteq V(G)\), let \(M_G(X)\) be the adjacency submatrix whose rows are indexed by \(X\) and columns by \(V(G)\setminus X\). Define the cut-rank
\[
\rho_G(X)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}M_G(X),
\]
where \(\mathbb F_2=\{0,1\}\) has addition and multiplication modulo two, and rank is the dimension of the row space over this field. A matrix with no rows or no columns has rank zero.

For \(n\ge2\), a rank decomposition consists of a finite tree \(T\) of maximum degree at most three and a bijection between its leaves and \(V(G)\). Removing any edge \(e\) partitions the leaves into two sets; write \(X_e\subseteq V(G)\) for either side. The width of the decomposition is \(\max_{e\in E(T)}\rho_G(X_e)\). This is independent of the chosen side because the two cut matrices are transposes. The rank-width \(\operatorname{rw}(G)\) is the minimum width over all such trees and leaf bijections. For \(n\le1\), set \(\operatorname{rw}(G)=0\). The unrooted decomposition convention here gives the same width as a rooted binary decomposition whose nodes represent the descendant leaf sets.

For a concrete input encoding, let \(\mathrm{bin}(n)\) be the ordinary binary expansion of \(n\), with \(\mathrm{bin}(0)=0\), and set \(b=|\mathrm{bin}(n)|\). Encode \(n\) by \(1^b0\,\mathrm{bin}(n)\), followed by the \(n^2\) adjacency bits in row-major order. Concatenate the two graph encodings. The machine must reject malformed strings; the displayed parameterized bound is required on valid graph pairs. The model charges every input access, tape move, arithmetic operation as its bit-level implementation, preprocessing step and output bit. No decomposition, parameter value, advice, oracle, randomness or uncharged preprocessing is available.

The program \(A\) and exponent \(c\) are fixed for all graph sizes and widths. The function \(f\) must be computable by an ordinary halting algorithm on every nonnegative integer, although it need not be polynomial, elementary or explicitly evaluated by \(A\). It may grow arbitrarily rapidly with the parameter. An algorithm with exponent depending on \(k\), or a separate nonuniform algorithm for each width without the stated common computable bound, is not the claimed fixed-parameter algorithm.

context_blocks.text: Question 6.2 contains two separate targets: fixed-parameter tractability and a smaller parameter-dependent polynomial exponent. This card retains the first branch. The survey defines fixed-parameter tractability with one algorithm and a computable parameter factor; the explicit bit encoding here makes that uniform convention concrete.

Grohe and Neuen give a polynomial-time isomorphism algorithm at every fixed rank-width, with running time \(O(n^{3k+5}\log n)\) for the stated bounded-width setting. The exponent still grows with \(k\). The revised paper corrects a proof issue in its earlier version; the cited revision is the July 2022 version.

The parallel canonization result gives small-depth circuits for each fixed rank-width, but their size has an exponent depending on the width. It does not supply the fixed exponent required by this card.

The 2026 connectivity-function result improves computation of rank-width and its decomposition. This is a different task from determining whether two graphs are isomorphic. The card charges any decomposition work done by its algorithm and does not assume one is given.

The survey also discusses isomorphism parameterized by rank-depth, which restricts the depth as well as the cut structure. Its cited fixed-parameter result is nonuniform and concerns the more restrictive parameter; it does not establish this rank-width target.

why: Rank-width captures dense graphs with structured adjacency cuts, extending the reach of graph decomposition beyond sparse settings. A uniform fixed-parameter isomorphism test would make the polynomial exponent independent of this structural complexity and settle a central boundary in parameterized graph isomorphism.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of the displayed existence proposition, including uniform correctness and the computable parameter factor, or a complete Lean proof of its logical negation. A conditional lower bound alone does not establish the unconditional negation. Polynomial time separately for each fixed width, efficient computation of a rank decomposition, or an algorithm for a more restrictive graph parameter is insufficient.

sentences: Rank-width measures the ranks of adjacency cuts in an optimally chosen decomposition tree.
Graph isomorphism asks whether a bijection of vertices preserves all edges.
This card asks for one deterministic algorithm whose polynomial exponent is independent of the rank-width.
The parameter-dependent multiplier may be any total computable function, and no decomposition is supplied.
Known fixed-width polynomial algorithms and faster decomposition methods do not by themselves give the required uniform isomorphism bound.
